relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a boy with PAPA syndrome carrying 'a heterozygous mutation in PSTPIP1 gene: c.748G>A(p.E250K)'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON. One in-scope patient (label 'patient', rule 5) plus three relatives tested negative ('his parents and younger brother'): parents labelled 'parent of patient' / 'parent of patient 2' (sex not stated), brother 'younger brother of patient'. Relatives have no variant or feature rows. Inheritance recorded as 'de novo' because both parents were tested negative, although the paper never uses the words 'de novo'. Table 1 is a timeline with episodes as columns (not patients); its (+)/(-) cells are defined in the legend but refer to single time points, so they were not used to exclude any feature for the person. Contradictions/uncertainties: the first sentence says he was diagnosed in August 2020 at nine years, but the genetic test and diagnosis are described in August 2017 with treatment 'after the diagnosis was confirmed' from September 2017; age at diagnosis recorded as 'nine-year-old' from the August 2020 sentence. The diagnosis sentence calls the genetic test 'abnormal' and zinc/MRP8/14 'nomal'; MRP8/14 (890.2 ng/mL) has no reference range printed, so its exclusion rests on the authors' statement that levels were normal. Subcutaneous purulent secretions (August 2016) recorded as a feature but the checklist item 'skin or soft-tissue abscesses' left not reported because the paper does not call it an abscess. 'MRI: Osteomyelitis' (2017/7) recorded as a feature, but 'sterile osteomyelitis or osteolytic bone lesions' left not reported because sterility of that lesion is not stated (treated with ceftriaxone). Normal WBC count and normal neutrophil ratio recorded as excluded abnormal WBC count / neutrophil ratio; neutropenia left not reported since absolute neutrophil count is not given as normal. Skin pustules are not called acne or pyoderma gangrenosum, so those checklist items are not reported. Anakinra dose is given as 300 mg qd in the Discussion; the duration of the anakinra gap differs between sections (from January 2020 vs 'for 3 months').

vital_status.span: Now, the child is in stable condition and has no new joint swellings

treatment_summary.value: Before diagnosis: articular incision and drainage, traditional Chinese medicine, topical glucocorticoid, intravenous cefotaxime and ceftriaxone, six free skin-flaps. After diagnosis: tocilizumab (5 mg/kg, five times) and IVIG (three times) without control; infliximab (5 mg/kg, nine times); anakinra from March 2019 for 10 months with no further joint symptoms; oral prednisolone acetate 20 mg from April 2020; thalidomide 25 mg nightly from August 2020, stable.
span: | Treatment | Articular incision and drainage | Articular incision and drainage | Traditional Chinese medicine | Topical glucocorticoid | Intravenous infusion of cefotaxime and the surgery of arthrotomy and drainage | Articular incision, intravenous infusion of cefotaxime, and a total of 6 times of free skin-flap successively | Intravenous infusion of ceftriaxone |
although he was given totally five times of tocilizumab (5 mg/kg) and three times of IVIG 10 g (400 mg/kg), the joint swelling still repeated
the patient has been treated with infliximab (5 mg/kg) for nine times
In March 2019, the anakinra was started to be used for 10 consecutive months, and no joint symptoms appeared after that

In April 2020, he started to take 20 mg prednisolone acetate orally at 8 o'clock each morning, and not only the symptoms were controlled, but also the IL-1, IL-6 and TNF-α values were generally rehabilitated to normal levels. In August 2020, he started to take 25 mg thalidomide orally once a night.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: Clinical history of cutaneous lesions and articular involvement plus genetic testing (heterozygous PSTPIP1 c.748G>A); normal zinc and MRP8/14 used to rule out Hz/Hc.
span: Given the patient's history of cutaneous lesions and articular involvement, the abnormal genetic testing, and the nomal serum levels of zinc and MRP8/14, the diagnosis of PAPA syndrome was made
In our study, the patient's serum MRP8/14 and zinc levels were normal. Thus, we ruled out the possibility of Hz/Hc.
